deities: Shiva (as Siddheshwar; ekamukha Shivalinga revered as Hari-Hara)

history.period: Last quarter of the 14th century AD per ASI/IGNCA monument report (CONFLICT: Google Arts & Culture says 14th century; a travel vlog claims 5th century Bhaumakara without evidence - verify)
history.summary: CONFLICT ON AGE (verify): the ASI monument record dates this Shiva temple to the last quarter of the 14th century AD (Eastern Ganga rule), with an attached 16th-century Bhrungaritesvara sub-shrine in the same complex. A travel vlog claims a 5th-century Bhaumakara origin with an inscription of King Subhakar Dev II, but this is not corroborated by the ASI record. The temple stands on the right bank of the Vaitarani river at Siddhesvara village, about 6 km from Jajpur town (off the Jajpur-Mangalpur road, 2.5 km from Sundureimuhan chowk). The presiding deity is a large ekamukha (one-faced) Shivalinga venerated as Hari-Hara, i.e. as both Vishnu and Shiva. The compound also holds fragmentary sculptures of gods, lions and female deities of the Somavamsi period, and the main shrine has a pidha vimana of Kalinga order. Coordinates are from the ASI/IGNCA monument report and are approximate.

name: Siddheshwar Temple
town_description: Siddhesvara is a small village on the right bank of the Vaitarani river in Jajpur district, about 6 km from Jajpur town along the Jajpur-Mangalpur road. It is one of the ancient sacred localities of the Jajpur-Viraja Kshetra region, dotted with Shiva shrines and fragmentary temple sculptures. Jajpur, the district headquarters, was the historic capital of the Somavamsi kingdom and is known as Viraja Kshetra, the sacred seat of Goddess Biraja.
